decisionsTitle: „Email respins” counts only the runner's own emails and keeps what the provider says (amending §663, §320, §653, §622, §76, §83)
decisionsSection:
**The owner, 2026-10-07**, on the production list of the 21 November race, two «Confirmată» cards (race numbers given) each carrying «Email respins» and «Retrimite QR»: «Cum e posibil să fie email respins dar și confirmat? Am nevoie de mai multe info in app». He had asked the same on 2026-10-04, and §663 answered it with words. This time the investigation read the data, and the data itself was wrong.

**What was found.**

1. **The club's own mail lit the runners' chip.** The declaration's archive copy (`DECLARATION_ARCHIVE`) and «somebody has confirmed» (`CLUB_CONFIRMATION_NOTICE`) are queued with the participant's id and registration but addressed to the club's mailboxes, and carry no club-copy flag; the chip's subquery left out only club copies (§320). A club mailbox that refused the archive copy marked the runner «Email respins» — on confirmed rows only, the ones that have an archive copy. The automatic re-send's refusal (§653) read the same rows.
2. **Mailgun refusing the club's account was stored as the runners' bounce.** Before §622 every permanent refusal at the send was `BOUNCED`; the refusals of 2026-10-01 and 02 (credentials, the probation's pause, the spent allowance's «recipient limit exceeded») still read as addresses that do not exist, and those runners really never got the message.
3. **Every permanent failure was a bad address.** A full mailbox, Mailgun's own suppression after an earlier bounce, a receiving server's policy and eight hours of deferrals were all stored `BOUNCED` and worded «adresa nu există sau căsuța e plină».
4. **Deliveries were thrown away.** `delivered` events were subscribed and discarded, so nothing ever cleared a refusal: the chip showed the newest refusal forever, whatever arrived after it.
5. **The webhook ignored whom an event was about.** One Mailgun message to an address and its Cc/Bcc shares one id, so a copy's failure marked the row.
6. **The webhook kept only Mailgun's one word.** The code, the server's words and the event's instant were thrown away.

**Decision: the stored facts are true and complete, and each registration has one email state.** The screens that draw it by cause, and the club's own side, are the next two changes, built on this one.

1. **Whom each message is for.** Every message type names its audience in one map (`notifications/domain/email-audience.ts`): the participant, the club's own mailboxes (the archive copies, the confirmation notice), the staff (invitations, the Administrators' notices) or the public (the newsletter, «registration is open», an invitation). A `Record` over the enum, so a type added tomorrow does not compile until somebody chooses; the club copies' rule (§320) and the privacy line (§323) now read it too, in place of two hand-kept sets. **Only a participant's own message — their type, their id on the row, not a club copy — says anything about them.**
2. **One migration, expand only** (`0131`): on `email_outbox`, `delivered_at`, `rejected_at`, `rejection_cause`, `provider_code`, `provider_detail`, `later_delivered_at`, `resolved_at`, `retried_at`, `retried_via`, all nullable, no CHECK (a value added later would be a contract); an index on `provider_message_id` (the webhook's lookup scanned the table) and one on `participant_id`. The backfill, once: the cause of every refusal written before, from the two shapes such rows have — Mailgun's one word, or the answer stored at the send — by the rule `rejectionCause` reads them with (a test runs the statement against the TypeScript on the same rows, the long answers among them as the send stored them, redacted and cut to 200 characters); the refusals and complaints already sent again (`retried_at`, `retried_via`, the latest send), and the account's refusals already over (`resolved_at`, the first send after). No delivery and no rejection instant is invented: none was recorded before.
3. **The webhook keeps what Mailgun said.** An event tagged for another deployment (`env:<APP_ENV>`, which the adapter now puts on every message) is answered without opening the database: QA and production share the sending domain and its webhooks. The row is found by the provider's id, else by its own idempotency key the message carried — only a row that left. The event's recipient is compared with the row's as spelled for delivery (`normalizedEmail`, never identity): an event for a copy on the archive's envelope leaves the row alone, logged with the row id only; a participant's message has no copies, so a respelling still lands; a `delivered` that names nobody changes nothing. `delivered` sets `delivered_at` once and never moves the status. A permanent failure is `BOUNCED` with its instant (Mailgun's `timestamp`, never later than now), cause, code and words, keeping `delivered_at` (a delayed bounce). A complaint is `COMPLAINED`, and a later bounce never overwrites it. **The provider's words are redacted before anything stores them** — one redactor, `infrastructure/email/redact.ts`, now the send's too: any address, the recipient's local part quoted alone, an IP literal, a token-length run, redacted first and cut to 200 characters after; the cause is read from the words before they are redacted, so a mailbox called «user» does not turn «User unknown» into nothing. Never the MX host, the sending IP, a geolocation or a client.
4. **What came after a refusal is kept on the refused row**, so the list reads it with one probe per row (`notifications/delivery-facts.ts`), under the participant's advisory lock and the same whichever event is processed first: a later delivery to the address sets `later_delivered_at` (the address works again — never on a complaint, never on the account's refusal); only the same message — its type, for the same registration — delivered later sets `resolved_at`: a delivered «Mesaj de la organizatori» does not give the runner the QR the bounced confirmation carried. The same message leaving again sets `retried_at` and `retried_via` — on a complaint too, which nothing else changes — and ends a refusal of the account; the send writes it in its own transaction under the same lock, so a refusal reported at the same moment and the send each read the other. `retried_at` is the **latest** such send, not the first the brief named: the state «sent again, delivery not known yet» is about the send whose delivery may still come, and its road must be that send's (a Gmail send after a Mailgun one never reports a delivery); the backfill keeps the same. A refusal at the send is stored with the same facts.
5. **Why, by a stated precedence** (`domain/rejection-cause.ts`), eleven causes stored by name: `no-such-address`, `mailbox-full`, `blocked`, `gave-up`, `refused`, `suppressed`, `unsubscribed`, `complained`, `complaint-suppressed`, `account`, `other`. The person's complaint (`complained`); Mailgun's suppressions (`suppress-*`, or the codes 605, 606, 607); a refusal at the send — the club's account unless it is the one 400 that names the address (the exact opposite of `classifyMailgunFailure`'s address case, with the redactor's `<address>` placeholder taken out first), and Gmail's 5.1.x; the enhanced status code, where a class-4 code decides only x.2.2 (a full mailbox — the last deferral a final `old` carries) and a class-5 code decides 5.1.x (no such address; 5.1.7 and 5.1.8 are the sender's, so blocked), 5.2.1 and 5.2.2 and 5.7.x (blocked) — so Yahoo's «421 4.7.0 [TSS04] … temporarily deferred» that ends in `old` is a give-up, not a block; Mailgun's reason (`old`, `greylisted` gave up; `espblock`, `blacklisted` blocked; `hardfail` no such address); the server's words (Yahoo's «This user doesn't have a yahoo.com account» and «This mailbox is disabled», Microsoft's «mailbox unavailable» and «Recipient not found» among them); a 552 the words said nothing more of; a plain `bounce` — `refused`, permanent, its cause not recorded and never read as «no such address»; else `other` (`generic` among them). The unit test reads the checklist's real strings — Yahoo's TSS04, 5.7.9, BL21, TSS09, 5.2.2 and its missing account, Microsoft's 5.5.0, 5.1.10, S3150 and 5.7.515, Gmail's refusal, Mailgun's suppressions and the account's refusals of 2026-10-01 and 02 as they were stored. A refusal written with no cause — by the deployment before this one, between the migration and the build after it — is classified when it is read, from its stored answer, by the same function; the answer never leaves the server.
6. **One email state per registration** (`registrations/email-state.ts`, `domain/email-state.ts`), chosen in SQL by one correlated subquery, so the list, the page, the desk, the filter and the export never disagree: **unreachable** — the address refuses the club's mail (a refusal with nothing delivered since, or a complaint), the registration's own or a family member's at the same event (§543: one address, one fact; another event's never); **not sent** — the club's account was refused when this message was to leave, and nothing left in its place; **missing** — the address works again, but this message has not arrived or been sent again; **retried** — sent again, no delivery known yet (by Gmail, never). The address first, then what is owed, then what waits; newest first within each. The list and the export read it without provider words; the desk its own projection — what did not arrive, why and when, the instants of what came after it included, never an address or the provider's words (§67); the registration's page alone reads the code and the redacted words. **Only the three that ask somebody to act — unreachable, not sent, missing — speak today**: «Doar cu un email respins» is one `EXISTS` over them, with a count read for its label (`countNeedingEmailActionForAdmin`); the chip, the page's red line and the export's `Email bounced` («Yes» or empty, the same column) show for them alone. `retried` waits for a delivery and is shown nowhere until the next change draws it: a refusal sent again before this release («Retrimite QR») will never be told its delivery, and a chip saying «Nu-l retrimite încă» on it forever would be the owner's complaint again. Until the next change draws the state by cause, the chip's words say which kind it is in one sentence — each kind its own, with its date when the reader has it and without it otherwise, never «the address does not exist» for an email that is merely owed — and what to do: call; send it again, said only to the Administrator who may (§289, `AGENTS.md` §15.11), and «ask an Administrator to send it again» to everybody else, the desk's every role included; wait. «Ce îi spui» says the address's refusal when the address refuses the club's mail, and «a club email has not reached you yet; we will send it again» for one the account could not send or one owed to an address that works again; it drops «look in spam» for every email refused and not sent again — none of them is in spam — and keeps it for a complaint and for an email sent again.
7. **The automatic re-send (§653)** is held back only by an address whose refusal still stands on the participant's own messages, for any event: a complaint, or a refusal with nothing delivered since. The club's mailboxes' refusals and the account's no longer hold the link back from a person whose address works. §653's «…for any event or a newsletter» loses its newsletter: a newsletter is the public's message, its row carries no participant, and the code never read it — `AGENTS.md` §16.2 now says so.
8. **The club's side reads** (`notifications/delivery-evidence.ts`, `countNeedingEmailActionByEvent`): every refusal of the club's own messages and of the club copies in the window, newest first, the limit applied in SQL, each with its role (the archive copy, the confirmation notice, a club copy) and the address only while it is still in the club's settings — a mailbox the club has since removed is listed by its role alone; whether Mailgun's deliveries arrive at all, as the participants' own messages that left by Mailgun in the last seven days against those of them delivered, bounded by `sent_at`; how many registrations of each upcoming event ask somebody to act. The registration's history (`listOutboxHistory`) reads newest first, every new column, the road, the role from the audience map and the club-copy flag — never a club mailbox's address — and the staff member who asked for a manual resend; today's rendering is unchanged but for the order. The person's own data (a GDPR access request, `person-data.ts`) carries each message's delivery, refusal, cause and later delivery, never the provider's words. The next change draws the club's reads, each behind its own server-side permission.
9. **Mailgun's webhook retries.** Mailgun retries a webhook it could not deliver for about eight hours (5, 10 and 15 minutes, then 1, 2 and 4 hours), but by its documentation's own wording not the delivery notification: a `delivered` event lost to a 5xx, a deployment or a cold start is never replayed, and the refusal it would have cleared stays until the same message is delivered again. Whether a retried event carries a fresh signature `timestamp` is not documented; if it does not, every retry after the signature's fifteen minutes (`mailgun-webhook.ts`) is refused with a 401 and lost. The check is kept as it is — weakening a replay guard on a guess is worse — and the question is the owner's.
10. **Documentation**: `AGENTS.md` §12.11 (the columns, the indexes, the audience), §16.2 (the re-send's refusal, and the newsletter clause's fate) and §16.5 (what the webhook does, and its retries); `SETUP.md` §35 step 5 — **«Delivered» is required**, both deployments' addresses on Delivered, Permanent Failure and Spam Complaints, and a lost delivery is not replayed — and the two lines that contradicted each other on where QA's events go.

**Privacy.** No change to the notice and nothing waits for one: it already says «Din fiecare mesaj păstrăm adresa, datele lui și starea trimiterii» and keeps a sent message's record ninety days and an undelivered one as long as the registration; a delivery's instant, a refusal's instant, cause, code and redacted words are the sending's state. `delivered` is the receiving server taking the message, not a read receipt: open and click tracking stay off (§320).

**Cost.** Production's webhook already received every `delivered` event and answered it before the database; each now writes once or twice, seconds after the send, while the compute is usually still awake — and QA's events no longer touch production's database at all.

**This amends** §663, which refused «storing a rejection instant» and said a later email that went through does not clear the chip — both reversed by the facts above; §76/§83 (the chip read any message type); §320 point 7 (the exclusion widens from the club copies to the club's own messages); §650 (the filter reads the state); §622 (the account's refusals stored `BOUNCED` before it read as the account's); §653 (the re-send's refusal).

**Refused.** Moving the account's old refusals to `FAILED` — a data rewrite that would put stale messages under «Reîncearcă emailurile eșuate»; they read as «not sent» instead. Recomputing a stored cause from `last_error` at read time — it is redacted and cut, and the rules changed (§622); only a row stored with none is read that way. Clearing a refusal by any later delivery. Clearing a complaint by a delivery. Inventing deliveries before this release. Comparing addresses with `lower()` for identity: the participant's id and the message type are the identity; the webhook compares how an address is spelled for delivery. A button that lifts an address from Mailgun's suppression list (an account-level key and a new secret), and a sending subdomain of QA's own, so its suppressions never touch production: not in this change.
changelogLine: - **«Email respins» tells the truth** — only a runner's own email that did not reach them marks the registration: a club mailbox refusing the archive copy or the confirmation notice, and Mailgun refusing the club's account on 1–2 October, no longer do. Mailgun's deliveries and its reasons are kept, so a refusal clears once the same email arrives, and the chip, the filter and the export speak only when somebody must act: the address refuses mail, the email never left, or it is owed to an address that works again — an email already sent again waits quietly. At the desk the words ask for an Administrator to resend. Mailgun's «Delivered» webhook is now required (SETUP §35). §NNN.

specsCriteria.text: Given a Mailgun event for another recipient of the same message (a copy on the envelope of the club's archive copy), when it is processed, then the row is unchanged and the log names the row's id alone; on a participant's message, which carries no copies, a respelled recipient still lands; a `delivered` event naming nobody changes nothing (2026-10-08, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

Given `delivered` for a row's own recipient, then `delivered_at` is set once and kept on a repeat and the status is unchanged; a permanent failure after it is `BOUNCED` with `delivered_at` kept; a complaint is never overwritten by a bounce (2026-10-08, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

Given a permanent failure, then the row keeps the event's instant (never later than now), its cause, its code and the receiving server's words redacted of any address, the recipient's local part, an IP literal and a token-length run, then cut to 200 characters — never the MX host, the sending IP, a geolocation or a client (2026-10-08, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

Given an event tagged for another deployment (`env:qa` on production's webhook, or the reverse), when it is received, then it is answered without opening the database; an untagged event is acted on as before (2026-10-08, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

Given a refusal of a participant's own message and a later delivery to the same address, then the refusal's `later_delivered_at` is the same whichever event was processed first; only the same message for the same registration delivered later sets `resolved_at`; a complaint and a refusal of the club's account are never cleared by a delivery (2026-10-08, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

Given a refusal at the send that is not the address's own — the account's credentials, the probation's pause, the spent allowance, the sender — whether stored before §622 or after, then it never counts against the address: the registration's state is «not sent» until the same message leaves again; the one 400 that names the address stays the address's (2026-10-08, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

Replaces criteria 48 and 49's «newest email». Given a registration, then «Email respins», the page's line under the address, the filter «Doar cu un email respins» and its count, and the export's `Email bounced` read one email state chosen from the participant's own messages only — never the club's archive copy, its confirmation notice or a club copy: the address refuses the club's mail (the registration's own refusal, or a family member's at the same event), the club's account refused it, the address works again but this email is owed, or it was sent again — in that order, the newest unresolved refusal first; they speak only for the first three, which ask somebody to act, and say nothing of an email sent again; the state ends when the same email is delivered, or for the account's refusal when it leaves (2026-10-08, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

Given the desk, the registrations list or the export, then none carries the provider's words or an address; only the registration's page reads the code and the redacted words, in small print (2026-10-08, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

Amends criterion 5. «Ce îi spui» adds the rejected email's sentence while the address refuses the club's mail, and for an email the club's account could not send, or one owed to an address that works again, says it has not reached them yet and will be sent again — never as the address's refusal; it drops the spam hint for every email refused and not sent again, and keeps it for a complaint and for an email sent again (2026-10-08, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

Amends criterion 8's «never to an address that bounced or complained on any message»: never to an address whose refusal still stands on any of the participant's own messages, for any event — a complaint, or a refusal with nothing delivered to the address since; a club mailbox's refusal and the club's Mailgun account refused at the send never hold it back (2026-10-08, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

Given a refusal, then its cause is stored by name — no-such-address, mailbox-full, blocked, gave-up, refused, suppressed, unsubscribed, complained, complaint-suppressed, account or other — by a stated precedence: a class-4 code decides only a full mailbox, so a final `old` after Yahoo's [TSS04] deferrals is gave-up; a plain `bounce` with no code is refused, never no-such-address; Yahoo's «doesn't have a yahoo.com account» is no-such-address; a row stored without a cause is classified when read, by the same function (2026-10-08, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

Given the desk, then «Email respins» says which email did not arrive, why and — for an email owed or sent again — since when, and asks every staff role but the Administrator to ask an Administrator to send it again; the registration's page tells the Administrator to send it again; neither says the address refused an email that is merely owed (2026-10-08, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

Given a registration's page, then its email history reads newest first, each row's role (the participant, the club's archive copy, the club's confirmation notice, a club copy) and never a club mailbox's address, the road, the delivery, the refusal with its cause and — on a refused row only — the code and the redacted words, what came after it, and the staff member who asked for a manual resend (2026-10-08, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

batchLine: «Email respins» tells the truth: the runners' own emails, Mailgun's facts kept, one email state that speaks only when somebody must act
